newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Analysts welcome new Alusuisse CEO.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome new Alusuisse CEO.

text.p: Chief finance officer Sergio Marchionne is the right man to lead Swiss aluminium, chemicals and packaging group Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG as new chief officer, analysts said on Tuesday.

Analysts said Marchionne, a 44-year-old Canadian citizen who joined Alusuisse in 1994, would bring continuity and an international financial perspective to the post when he succeeds Theodor Tschopp next April 2.
Alusuisse announced earlier that Marchionne would rise from finance officer when Tschopp makes a long-planned move to chairman of the board at next year's annual shareholder meeting.
"Marchionne is the right man," said Werner Richli at CS Research in Zurich.
"He is relatively young, dynamic, very unconvetional and has a lot of drive. He has a lot of toughnes and sees things from a financial point of view," Richli told Reuters.

Richli also said Marchionne would have a fair approach to the group's wide-ranging international business, which is present in most industrial countries, becuase of his trans-Atlantic persepctive as a Canadian in Switzerland.
"He is not rooted in Swiss conditions and does not depend on Swiss networks," Richli noted.
Michel Kamm at Union Bancaire Privee in Geneva said Marchionne would provide continuity for the group.
"Marchionne is quiet well know to the financial markets. This is an unspectacular transition," he said.
Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) analyst Ivo Hanusch said Marchionne appointment was very positive because the finance officer knew the company well.
Marchionne was one of the key executives who worked out a new strategy since 1994 of concentrating on increasing value by growing divisions with high value-added potential.
"He's not just a man of figures but was also instrumental in implementing the new strategy," Hanusch said.
